elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) prohibits Company-payable termination payments, liquidated damages, and penalties only “in the event the Company terminates this Agreement,” rather than imposing an unconditional prohibition for all triggers.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The clause does not establish that every possible Company-payable liquidated amount may arise only as an early-termination fee; it only negates amounts when the Company terminates.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No three-month cap appears, and Section 4.2(c) continues to contemplate a possible Termination Payment without such a cap.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not state that an early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company.
